note: The `bmar` (Барыги) PURCHASE arms for menu rows 1..6 -- what happens after the row key is typed at the `^0Барыги\` prompt, not what the menu prints. The menu half is `data/shops.json` / `docs/re/tables.md` §2; rows 7..9 were mapped by Task 18. All nine `bmar` arms are ported and live in `Game::buy_dealer_row` (Task 24; `Game::buy_pistol_row` was that function's name until it grew rows 1..6, and nothing answers to it now). Prose twin: `docs/re/shop-arms.md`. Re-derived from `orig/g.exe` by `tools/test_shop_arms.py`; nothing here was read off a screen. The `mar` (Базар) shop's nine arms are the sibling block under the top-level `mar` key, mapped by Task 25; the two were measured over their own ranges and neither's findings were inferred from the other's.
address_forms: `1000:xxxx` is a Ghidra label (Form A of `docs/re/METHODOLOGY.md`) and, because the game's code segment is the load base, its OFF is also the image offset. `20ae:xxxx` is DGROUP. `cs_offset` is the image offset of a Pascal shortstring's LENGTH byte -- the exact immediate of the `mov di,imm16` that pushes it -- and `file_offset` is that plus the 0x18d0-byte MZ header, which is what `data/strings.json` keys on.
globals_exclude: 20ae:38c7, the player's money, is written by every arm and referenced 107 times across the image; `docs/re/tables.md` § "Other price sources" already owns that population, so `globals[]` does not restate it per row.

rows_bounded_on_the_right_by.note: Row 6's miss lands on 1000:ccc4, whose own six-instruction setup feeds the compare at 1000:ccce against the literal `7` -- Task 18's first row. That is what bounds the rows-1..6 range on the right without assuming it. 1000:ccd8, which three earlier documents called row 7's key compare, is its already-own gate; see `docs/re/gaps.md`.

input_read.note: One line is read, then every row's compare runs against it in turn: each row's miss branch targets the NEXT row's setup, and each arm's tail jumps there too. So the arms are a chain of independent `if`s over one buffer, the same shape `docs/re/combat-dispatch.md` records for the `Битва\` prompt.

district_finding.claim: No arm of `bmar` rows 1..6 tests the district byte `20ae:3692` at all.
district_finding.method: The whole span decodes as one aligned run (474 instructions from `1000:c8ce`, the row-1 setup, to `1000:ccc4`, the row-7 setup). No instruction in it carries a direct-memory operand whose value is 0x3692, and the byte pair `92 36` does not occur in the span at all -- so there is not even a byte-scan candidate to discard.

district_gates_sweep_range.note: The `bmar` verb compare to the start of row 7's already-own gate -- the whole handler up to Task 18's block. `district_gates_are_menu_only` is asserted SET-EQUAL to every `cmp byte [0x3692],imm` site an aligned decode of this range finds, so an omitted entry reds the test. An earlier revision of this artifact listed two of the five and called that `the two district gates that exist in this handler`; the sweep exists because that claim was guarded by nothing.

rows_7_9_arms_carry_no_district_test_eit.method: The row-7 setup to the `x` compare at 1000:ce80 -- i.e. all three of Task 18's arms. An aligned decode of that range carries no operand equal to 0x3692 and the byte pair `92 36` does not occur in it, by the same two measurements used on rows 1..6.
rows_7_9_arms_carry_no_district_test_eit.consequence: The buy path of the dealers carries no district test at ALL, for any of the nine rows. When this was written the port refused all five gated rows, so the divergence was the whole path and not two rows; Task 24 closed it for every one of the five. The measurement above is a fact about `orig/g.exe` and is unchanged by that.

district_finding.consequence: At district 1 the menu prints neither row 5 nor row 6, but typing `5` or `6` still buys them; the same holds for rows 7..9 below district 4. The port reproduced this in Task 24 (commits 19a1a34, fef8c9c): the menu's district filter is `Game::listed_rows`, called only by `Game::print_priced_rows`, and `Game::shop_action` delegates to `Game::buy_dealer_row` BEFORE it consults `Game::gate_open`, consulting it afterwards only on the `mar` path (`grep -n 'self.gate_open' src/game.rs` returns exactly those two call sites). Until Task 24 the port called `gate_open` ahead of the delegation and refused all five gated rows; that is the divergence this field used to record as open. Nothing here is claimed about the `mar` shop -- that range was not decoded for this task.

mar.note: The `mar` (Базар, the market) PURCHASE arms for menu rows 1..9 -- what happens after the row key is typed at the `^0Базар\` prompt, not what the menu prints. The menu half is `data/shops.json` / `docs/re/tables.md` §2. The market pickpocket block that follows row 9 (`1000:c353`..`1000:c369`, `docs/re/gaps.md`) is deliberately NOT mapped here. rows_bounded_on_the_right_by.note: Row 9's miss lands on 1000:c31f, whose own six-instruction setup feeds the compare at 1000:c329 against the literal `t` -- the market pickpocket verb, whose block is out of this task's scope. That is what bounds the nine rows on the right without assuming it.

input_read.note: The same one-buffer chain-of-ifs shape `bmar` uses: one line is read at 1000:bd43 into 20ae:3a72, then each row compares that one buffer against its own one-character CS literal with Borland's shortstring compare 0f78:0bd8, and each row's miss branch targets the next row's span start. Three rows differ from every `bmar` row: rows 6, 8 and 9 have a district gate in FRONT of their setup, so the row's span starts at the gate rather than at the `mov di,0x3a72`.

district_finding.claim: Three of the nine `mar` arms DO test the district byte 20ae:3692, and they test it BEFORE the row's key compare -- so below the district the row is not refused, it is unreachable, and no message is printed. This is the opposite of `bmar`, whose buy path carries no district test at any of its nine rows.
district_finding.method: The whole span decodes as one aligned run of 696 instructions -- 1000:bd48, the row-1 setup, to 1000:c31f, the setup for the compare at 1000:c329 that follows row 9. Every instruction in it carrying a direct-memory operand equal to 0x3692 is listed in `buy_path_gates`, asserted SET-EQUAL rather than spot-checked, and the raw `92 36` byte-pair count over the same span is asserted to match, so neither the positive nor the negative rests on the decoder alone.

sweep_range.note: The `mar` verb compare to the end of row 9's arm -- i.e. the menu-print block AND the nine arms, and nothing else. `buy_path_gates` + `menu_gates` is asserted set-equal to every `[0x3692]` operand an aligned decode of this range finds, and to a raw `92 36` byte scan over it, so an omitted gate reds `tools/test_shop_arms.py`. The three further `[0x3692]` reads in the image at 1000:c333, 1000:c3a0 and 1000:c3b9 are the market pickpocket block, which starts at 1000:c31f and is out of this task's scope -- the range end is what excludes them, not a filter.

price_byte_range.note: The nine `mar` price bytes, one per row, in key order. Used to measure which MENU lines each menu gate covers: the `mov al,[price]` operands an aligned decode of the gate's listed_from..skip_target range finds, restricted to this range so the colour byte 20ae:3b7a that the same range also loads is not mistaken for a row.

row_7_is_menu_gated_but_not_buy_gated.claim: Row 7 (adidas, 30 руб.) is hidden from the menu below district 2 and sold anyway. The menu gate at 1000:bb80 covers TWO menu lines -- rows 6 and 7 both load their price byte between its fall-through 1000:bb8a and its skip target 1000:bc42 -- while the buy path has a district gate only in front of row 6. Row 7's span starts at 1000:c142, which is exactly where row 6's district gate jumps when it skips (1000:c095 jmp 0xc142), and 1000:c142 is the `mov di,0x3a72` setup itself: no district test stands between the skip and row 7's key compare at 1000:c14c.
row_7_is_menu_gated_but_not_buy_gated.consequence: At district 1 the market lists rows 1..5 and no more; typing `6` falls through to the re-prompt without a word, and typing `7` buys the adidas suit for 30 руб. and applies its armour bonus. Rows 8 and 9 do have their own buy-path gates and are genuinely unreachable below districts 3 and 4.

district_finding.contrast_with_bmar: `bmar`'s five district gates are ALL menu-print gates and its buy path has none (`district_finding` above, and `bugs[].row-5-and-6-are-buyable-below-their-menu-district`). `mar` is the other shape for three of its four gated rows and the `bmar` shape for the fourth. Neither shop's finding was inferred from the other's; each was measured over its own range.

bugs.label: mar-district-gates-refuse-silently
bugs.claim: The three `mar` buy-path district gates print NOTHING. Each sits in front of its row's SETUP, so below the district the key compare never runs: 1000:c095, 1000:c1de and 1000:c286 jump straight to the row's own span end, which is the next row's span start. Typing `6` at district 1 prints no message at all -- not a refusal, not an echo; the line falls through every remaining compare to 1000:c47b, the handler's own re-prompt, exactly as an unrecognised key does. `bmar` has one comparable shape, row 9's first two gates, which the port already reproduces.

bugs.label: mar-upgrade-rows-grant-the-delta-not-the-bonus
bugs.claim: Rows 7, 8 and 9 each test the LESSER item's flag and grant only the DIFFERENCE when it is already owned: adidas +1 instead of +2 (guard 1000:c1aa, branch 1000:c1af), the better boots +1/+1 instead of +2/+2 (1000:c249 / 1000:c24e), the better jacket +2 instead of +4 (1000:c2f1 / 1000:c2f6). So the armour or damage a player ends up with is the same whichever order the two rows are bought in. Not a bug; recorded because reproducing it needs the guard, not just the add -- an arm that always added the full bonus would double-count the upgrade. CORROBORATION, not part of this task's decode: the gym's armour-scratch recompute subtracts exactly those totals (1 for 20ae:38b4 alone, 2 for 20ae:38b7, 2 for 20ae:38b6 alone, 4 for 20ae:38b9), which `docs/re/gaps.md` already established from 1000:e3a4..1000:e3e2 and which nothing here re-derives.

where.delta_rejoins_note: The unconditional jump that carries the DELTA arm past the full-bonus arm, one per row. Recorded because `docs/re/shop-arms.md` shows these three splits as fenced code blocks and the prose checker strips fences, so their identity is checked here instead.
